title: Flame spread: Effects of microgravity and scale
summary: Demonstrated that large-scale microgravity flame spread behaves differently from terrestrial upward flame spread and that experiment scale and forced flow matter substantially.
relevance: Key foundation showing small-scale 1g tests fail to predict large spacecraft fire spread.

title: Opposed-flow flame spread: A comparison of microgravity and normal gravity experiments to establish the thermal regime
summary: Compares ISS BASS-II PMMA experiments with normal-gravity data, demonstrating why terrestrial intuition cannot simply be transferred to spacecraft habitats.
relevance: Validates PMMA flame quenching and spherical flame front dynamics at low airflow.

title: Experimental study of concurrent-flow flame spread over thin solids in confined space in microgravity
summary: Investigates airflow, oxygen, and confinement effects on flame spread inside duct geometries in microgravity.
relevance: Justifies enclosure and airflow filters for spacecraft avionics compartment safety.

title: Burning in microgravity: Experimental results and analysis
summary: Covers 59 successfully ignited tests across varying oxygen and pressure conditions, providing strong structured comparison data.
relevance: Quantifies oxygen index limits for polymers in microgravity.

title: Numerical study of the effects of confinement on large-scale fires in microgravity
summary: Demonstrates that enclosure geometry materially affects flame-spread behavior rather than being a background detail.
relevance: Shows confinement accelerates flame growth by preventing convective thermal escape.

title: Dynamics of flame spread over filter papers in microgravity aboard the ISS
summary: Reports flame-spread behavior close to flammability limits aboard ISS and illustrates why sustained-microgravity empirical evidence remains essential.
relevance: Recent 2026 empirical data demonstrating near-limit microgravity flammability.
